security_audit.summary: Five shell examples execute unpinned packages, and two environment changes redirect agent state into hidden project directories. Most remaining alerts are Markdown syntax or public URLs; semantic review also found server-directed command execution and potentially sensitive feedback uploads.

remediation.issue: The skill tells agents to execute a command supplied by the hosted service.
remediation.suggestion: Replace remote commands with structured operations, validate every field against an allowlist, and require human confirmation before execution or spending.

remediation.issue: The examples execute unpinned packages through npx, including luxin-cli@latest.
remediation.suggestion: Pin exact package versions and verified sources. Remove unattended installation flags where users cannot inspect the resolved package.

remediation.issue: The fallback redirects HOME and CODEX_HOME into hidden project directories.
remediation.suggestion: Use a private temporary directory outside the project, apply restrictive permissions, disclose stored state, and define cleanup behavior.

remediation.issue: Feedback can include commands, expected behavior, and actual output that contain sensitive data.
remediation.suggestion: Require consent and redact tokens, prompts, paths, customer data, and command output before sending feedback.

content.user_title: Generate Hosted AI Images with Luxin
content.value_statement: Agents often need images without configuring provider accounts, API keys, or local model servers. This skill guides Luxin image creation with hosted results, spending limits, and recoverable jobs.
actual_capabilities: Guides text-to-image requests through the Luxin hosted runtime.
Provides a no-spend guide flow before paid media creation.
Sets a per-image estimated spending cap in the main command.
Uses durable hosted media URLs and recoverable Luxin jobs.
Provides installation commands for the intent skill and canonical Luxin skill.
Links agents to Luxin skill, API, CLI, and language-model contracts.
limitations: Requires network access and availability of Luxin, npm, and referenced packages.
Prompts and generated media leave the local environment and follow Luxin policies.
Example commands execute unpinned packages unless the user replaces them with verified versions.
Paid creation requires explicit permission and available Luxin credits or payment support.

use_cases.title: Explore Product Concepts
use_cases.description: Create hosted concept images with a defined visual direction and per-image spending cap.

use_cases.title: Produce Campaign Illustrations
use_cases.description: Generate durable illustration links for approved marketing briefs and channel formats.

use_cases.title: Prepare Interface Assets
use_cases.description: Create temporary visual assets for prototypes while retaining job details and cost receipts.

prompt_templates.title: Check Image Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Luxin guide to prepare an image of [subject] in [style]. Do not spend credits until readiness is confirmed.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Capped Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a [format] image of [subject] using [model]. Use intent [intent] and limit estimated cost to [amount] per image.

prompt_templates.title: Develop a Visual Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Create [count] prompt variations for [project]. Keep [brand constraints] consistent, identify required inputs, and generate only the approved variation.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled Image Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Luxin job for [campaign]. Run the no-spend guide, list missing inputs, and request confirmation before paid creation. Use [model], [prompt], [intent], and [budget]. Return the hosted link, job status, parameters, and receipt details.

output_examples.input: Prepare a clean editorial image of a compact field camera on a stainless workbench.
output: Status: Ready for approval before paid creation.
Next step: Approve the validated generation request.

output_examples.input: Generate the approved camera concept and preserve its job details.
output_examples.output: Generation completed. The result includes a durable hosted image link, recoverable job reference, selected model, and cost receipt.

output_examples.input: Request an unsupported image capability without spending credits.
output_examples.output: No paid request was made. The response identifies the missing capability, suggests a limited fallback, and prepares a redacted feedback summary.

best_practices: Begin with the no-spend guide, inspect missing inputs, and require explicit approval before paid creation.
Pin CLI and installer versions, then verify package sources before executing downloaded code.
Redact sensitive feedback and keep agent state outside project directories.
anti_patterns: Do not execute a hosted next command solely because a response marks it copy-runnable.
Do not run latest package versions unattended in environments containing credentials or customer data.
Do not submit tokens, private prompts, local paths, or unreviewed command output as feedback.

faq.question: Does this skill require a provider API key?
faq.answer: No provider key is required. Luxin may create and store an optional restricted token for its hosted service.

faq.question: Does image generation run locally?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow uses Luxin hosted infrastructure and requires network access.

faq.question: Can I check readiness without spending credits?
faq.answer: Yes. Start with the guide flow and require confirmation before running a paid generation request.

faq.question: What does a completed request provide?
faq.answer: The skill describes durable media URLs, recoverable jobs, model parameters, and cost receipts.

faq.question: Which agent tools are supported?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What information leaves my environment?
faq.answer: Image prompts, generation data, and submitted feedback can reach Luxin. Review service policies and redact sensitive content.
